R572.note: Moves the last_write_ptr assignment to after the realloc growth block so it always addresses the live allocation; nothing else changes.

R573.note: secrets.token_urlsafe(32) closes the weak-PRNG vector, but returns a 43-character string containing '-' and '_', breaking the stated 32-character alphanumeric contract without the write-up stating the length/charset change (secrets.choice over the existing alphabet would have preserved it).

R574.note: Server-defined maps for column and direction with canonical values reaching ORDER BY; accountId stays parameterized, defaults preserved, lowercase dir still accepted, and the silent fallback for unknown keys is stated.

R575.note: Applies the existing HTML-escaping helper to rawComment at the point of HTML assembly; only the rename and the added escape call change.

R576.note: Path.GetRelativePath component-based containment rejects '..'-prefixed and rooted results, closing the sibling-directory prefix bypass while keeping the same Forbid/NotFound shape.

R577.note: Template source becomes a constant and the term is passed as a Jinja context variable, so Flask autoescaping applies and the SSTI path is closed too; page structure unchanged.

R578.note: Replaces the variable-variable call with a fixed dispatch table of the two intended commands; unknown names return a message rather than reaching any call.

R579.note: Rejects keys containing whitespace/control bytes or exceeding 250 bytes before building the set line - the same constraints memcached itself enforces, so no legitimate key is blocked; the new exception is stated.

R580.note: Adds the same can:update,order policy middleware the sibling mutating routes use; the assumption that update is the right ability is stated openly.

R581.note: session_regenerate_id(true) immediately before writing authenticated state; credential checks and return values untouched.

R582.note: Plaintext listener now serves only a redirect-to-HTTPS handler as the file's own comment says it was meant to, so the unprotected mux is unreachable; the change is stated plainly (minor nit: r.Host carries a non-standard port into the redirect).

R583.note: createCipheriv with a per-request scrypt-derived key, random salt and random IV; the added non-secret salt/iv response fields are inherent to the fix and stated plainly with the decrypt-side follow-up.

R584.note: Dropping the request-derived Entity map closes the vector, but with Entity nil Go's strict decoder now rejects any document referencing ¬eLabel; with a 400 (reproduced in a scratch directory with go1.25), which the write-up presents as 'no reliance' rather than stating as breakage, and the added 1 MiB body cap is a new limit.

R585.note: crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('base64url') replaces Math.random; the code is opaque to the rest of the handler and the longer base64url format is stated, with storage and response shape unchanged.
